regions.merged_text: God bless you and yours -- Aye and -- including this poor plodder. I surely hope you keep well. Thanks be to God we are well down here. We've had a very mild Winter, hardly any snow to speak of and practically no colds. All this, not- withstanding quite a lot of rain and early in the week a visita- tion of sleet and freezing rain that in quite a few places shrubs and trees were loaded down to breaking down. The inclosed telegram came the night before last and Grace phoned yesterday morning giving more particulars and asking that I let you know about the situation. Bernard, Sr. had been out on some official busines in Eureka, was quite occupied Thursday evening so that he neglected some kind of a natural call to which he was not as promptly obedient as Grandmother Nature often has to insist on. So he had to go to the hospital for treatment. Grace did not seem to think it very serious coparatively. We hope of course that it was not serious. However, they are right -- we do right rather -- to pray that nothing serious come of such experiences. Otherwise every one seems to be holding their own on the Coast. How can we ever be thankful as we ought to be! Glory be to God. Inclosed is also a letter from poor, dear Brother Pat. He too seems well and, glad to see, still retains a coloring of favorable humor. I should have had this off yesterday morning, as I told Grace I would and by all means meant to do. ... Please pardon.
